speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions and tell me if you have any joint swelling or pain in areas other than your wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall noticing a large, expanding rash at the site of a tick bite during your camping trip in Minnesota? Have you experienced any headaches, fatigue, or facial weakness (such as difficulty closing one eye) since returning?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip to Minnesota and the specific appearance of your lesions, I suspect a tick-borne illness. REQUEST TEST: PCR for Ehrlichia and Anaplasma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative PCR for Ehrlichia and Anaplasma, I need to rule out other tick-borne infections common in Minnesota, such as Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever or Lyme disease. REQUEST TEST: PCR for Rickettsia rickettsii and Borrelia burgdorferi.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative tick-borne panels and the presence of painful wrist swelling with violaceous vesiculopustular lesions, I need to rule out septic arthritis and gonococcal infection. REQUEST TEST: Joint aspiration for Gram stain and culture, and NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint Aspiration Left Wrist: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen; STI Screen (NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae): Positive

speaker: Doctor
text: The joint aspiration showing Gram-negative diplococci and the positive NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae confirm the diagnosis of disseminated gonococcal infection. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
